summary: Laos admits nationals of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam visa-free for up to 30 days (Myanmar for 14), plus Japan, South Korea, Russia, Switzerland and others on bilateral or unilateral waivers. Nearly everyone else can get a 30-day tourist visa — online through the official Lao eVisa or on arrival at major airports and border crossings. The eVisa list names 162 countries and territories (as of 8 October 2026); for nationalities not on it, mostly in Africa and the Middle East plus Pakistan, Bangladesh and Iran, no official source we could read states how they get a visa.

notes: The UK FCDO says Laos has zero tolerance for drug offences, including cannabis: possessing even very small quantities carries severe penalties, and drug trafficking can carry the death penalty.
The UK FCDO says e-cigarettes (vapes), heated tobacco and shisha are illegal in Laos: importing, possessing, using, buying or selling them can bring a fine or prison.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says travellers regularly report random bag snatches, often by people on motorcycles, and that petty crime can occur in tourist areas and around ATMs. It advises against all but essential travel to Xaisomboun Province, where there have been attacks on infrastructure and armed clashes with anti-government groups. It says landmines and unexploded weapons are a hazard throughout Laos and advises keeping to main routes in rural areas.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says US dollars and Thai baht are commonly accepted in Laos, and that the kip is not easily obtained or exchanged outside the country.

The Lao eVisa is accepted only at nine designated ports: Wattay (Vientiane), Luang Prabang and Pakse international airports, Lao-Thai Friendship Bridges I, II and IV, Boten International Checkpoint, and Boten and Khamsavath railway stations. At any other port you need a visa on arrival, and the eVisa fee is not refunded.

The UK FCDO says landmines and other unexploded weapons are a hazard throughout Laos and kill people each year; Canada names the Plain of Jars, Xiengkhouang province and the Lao-Vietnam border areas in particular. The FCDO advises keeping to main routes in rural areas and not picking up metal objects.
The UK FCDO says both men and women should cover their shoulders and knees when visiting temples and religious sites, and that walking around in public in swimwear is not culturally appropriate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: Nationals of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam enter visa-free for up to 30 days and Myanmar nationals for 14, and Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Russia and Mongolia have bilateral or unilateral waivers. Almost everyone else — including US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passport holders — gets a 30-day tourist visa either online via laoevisa.gov.la or on arrival at major entry points. For nationalities missing from the eVisa list, no official source we could read states how to get a visa.

faq.question: Should I get the Lao eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Both give a 30-day single-entry tourist stay. The eVisa (USD 50, about three business days online) skips the arrival line but is accepted only at designated checkpoints; the visa on arrival is issued at major entry points, such as international airports and border crossings. No official page publishes its fee.

faq.question: Can I use the Lao eVisa at any border crossing?
faq.answer: No. It is honored only at designated entry points, including Vientiane's Wattay and Luang Prabang international airports and the first Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge. The eVisa portal says that at any other port you must get a visa on arrival, and the eVisa fee is not refunded.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. Tourist visas can be extended at most twice per arrival at the Department of Immigration in Vientiane (the Department's visa page says a visa on arrival can be extended once); no maximum length per extension is published. Apply at least 3 days before your stay expires; the fee is 20,000 kip per day plus 40,000 kip per application, and it takes 1-2 business days. Visa-exempt stays cannot be extended except in emergencies, with supporting documents.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders are not visa-exempt. Apply online for the Lao eVisa (USD 50) before travel or obtain a 30-day tourist visa on arrival at major airports and border crossings.
